# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
_This was originally posted on our Voronoi app. Download the app for free on iOS or Android and discover incredible data-driven charts from a variety of trusted sources._
Humanity may have never finished building the Tower of Babel, but that hasn’t stopped us from building towering skyscrapers and magnificent monuments, particularly in the post-Industrial era.
How tall have these structures gotten? And when were they built?
We visualize the tallest statue on every continent (excluding Antarctica), along with where they are located and the year of its completion. Important to note: the height measurements include the foundation. Data is from a list of sources: World Famous Things, World Atlas, the Guinness World Records, and Britannica.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## Ranked: Towering Statues, by Continent
At a colossal 182 meters (597 ft), the **Statue of Unity** is the tallest in Asia—and the world—and is located in the Indian state of Gujarat.
| Statue Name | Country | Continent | Height |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Statue of Unity | 🇮🇳 India | Asia | 182m |  
| Sanctuary of Christ the King (Santuário Nacional de Cristo Rei) | 🇵🇹 Portugal | Europe | 110m |  
| Statue of Liberty | 🇺🇸 USA | North America | 93m |  
| Monument de la Renaissance Africaine (African Renaissance Monument) | 🇸🇳 Senegal | Africa | 52m |  
| Monumento a la Virgen de la Paz (Monument to the Virgin of Peace) | 🇻🇪 Venezuela | South America | 47m |  
| Big Merino | 🇦🇺 Australia | Oceania | 15m |
Completed in 2018, it depicts Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, a key leader in the Indian Independence movement and India’s first deputy Prime Minister. His legacy—the political integration of India—lends the statue its name.
Portugal’s **Sanctuary of Christ the King** is the tallest in Europe, at 110 meters (361 ft). Inspired by Christ the Redeemer in Rio, the statue was completed in 1959 as an expression of gratitude for Portugal not suffering direct consequences from World War II.
Across the Atlantic, NYC’s famous **Statue of Liberty** is the tallest in North America at 93 meters (305 ft). A gift from the people of France, the structure originally shone a reddish-brown color. The current green visage is the result of the natural oxidation of its copper surfaces.
Rounding up, Senegal’s **African Renaissance Monument** (52m / 171 ft) and Venezuela’s **Monument to the Virgin of Peace** (47m / 154 ft) are the tallest in Africa and South America respectively.

The Philippines, Brazil, and Turkey are the only three markets where internet users average more than 10 hours of gaming per week. Brazil comes in second at 10 hours and 56 minutes, followed by Turkey at 10 hours and 11 minutes.
For Filipino internet users, the weekly figure works out to roughly 1 hour and 36 minutes of gaming per day, more than 35 minutes above the worldwide daily average.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## Brazil and Mexico Outgame U.S. Despite Massive Gaming Market
The Americas account for five of the top 10 markets, making the region particularly prominent in the ranking.
Brazil averages nearly two hours more gaming per week than the United States, while Mexico also ranks ahead of the U.S. at 9 hours and 24 minutes.
This contrasts with the U.S. being the world’s second-largest video game market by revenue in 2024, highlighting the difference between a country’s gaming market size and the time its internet users spend playing.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## East Asia Shapes Gaming Culture, But Spends Less Time Playing
Some of the most surprising results come from East Asia, home to several of the world’s most influential video game industries.
South Korea averages 5 hours and 48 minutes of gaming per week, while China records 5 hours and 12 minutes. Taiwan comes in at 6 hours and 3 minutes, and Hong Kong at 5 hours and 6 minutes.
Japan ranks 53rd out of 54 markets, with internet users spending just 3 hours and 59 minutes gaming each week. That’s less than half the 9 hours and 9 minutes recorded in the United States.
Despite their global influence on gaming culture, all five East Asian markets fall below the worldwide average.
Japan’s position is particularly striking given its role in shaping the global gaming industry through companies such as Nintendo and Sony.
The contrast highlights an important distinction: producing some of the world’s most influential video games doesn’t necessarily mean spending the most time playing them.

_This was originally posted on our Voronoi app. Download the app for free on iOS or Android and discover incredible data-driven charts from a variety of trusted sources._
Humanity may have never finished building the Tower of Babel, but that hasn’t stopped us from building towering skyscrapers and magnificent monuments, particularly in the post-Industrial era.
How tall have these structures gotten? And when were they built?
We visualize the tallest statue on every continent (excluding Antarctica), along with where they are located and the year of its completion. Important to note: the height measurements include the foundation. Data is from a list of sources: World Famous Things, World Atlas, the Guinness World Records, and Britannica.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## Ranked: Towering Statues, by Continent
At a colossal 182 meters (597 ft), the **Statue of Unity** is the tallest in Asia—and the world—and is located in the Indian state of Gujarat.
| Statue Name | Country | Continent | Height |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Statue of Unity | 🇮🇳 India | Asia | 182m |  
| Sanctuary of Christ the King (Santuário Nacional de Cristo Rei) | 🇵🇹 Portugal | Europe | 110m |  
| Statue of Liberty | 🇺🇸 USA | North America | 93m |  
| Monument de la Renaissance Africaine (African Renaissance Monument) | 🇸🇳 Senegal | Africa | 52m |  
| Monumento a la Virgen de la Paz (Monument to the Virgin of Peace) | 🇻🇪 Venezuela | South America | 47m |  
| Big Merino | 🇦🇺 Australia | Oceania | 15m |
Completed in 2018, it depicts Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, a key leader in the Indian Independence movement and India’s first deputy Prime Minister. His legacy—the political integration of India—lends the statue its name.
Portugal’s **Sanctuary of Christ the King** is the tallest in Europe, at 110 meters (361 ft). Inspired by Christ the Redeemer in Rio, the statue was completed in 1959 as an expression of gratitude for Portugal not suffering direct consequences from World War II.
Across the Atlantic, NYC’s famous **Statue of Liberty** is the tallest in North America at 93 meters (305 ft). A gift from the people of France, the structure originally shone a reddish-brown color. The current green visage is the result of the natural oxidation of its copper surfaces.
Rounding up, Senegal’s **African Renaissance Monument** (52m / 171 ft) and Venezuela’s **Monument to the Virgin of Peace** (47m / 154 ft) are the tallest in Africa and South America respectively.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## Which Countries Spend the Most Time Playing Video Games?
### Key Takeaways
*   The Philippines leads the ranking, with internet users spending an average of 11 hours and 14 minutes gaming each week.  
*   Five of the top 10 markets are in the Americas, including Brazil, Mexico, the United States, Chile, and Argentina.  
*   All five East Asian markets surveyed, including Japan, China, and South Korea, rank below the worldwide average for weekly gaming time.
From mobile games to consoles and PCs, gaming is a global pastime. But which countries spend the most time playing, and how do some of the world’s biggest gaming markets compare?
This visualization ranks 54 countries and territories by weekly gaming time using data from GWI’s Q2 2025 research, published in the Digital 2026 Global Overview Report. The figures cover internet users aged 16 and older and include mobile, console, and computer gaming.

For Filipino internet users, the weekly figure works out to roughly 1 hour and 36 minutes of gaming per day, more than 35 minutes above the worldwide daily average.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## Brazil and Mexico Outgame U.S. Despite Massive Gaming Market
The Americas account for five of the top 10 markets, making the region particularly prominent in the ranking.
Brazil averages nearly two hours more gaming per week than the United States, while Mexico also ranks ahead of the U.S. at 9 hours and 24 minutes.
This contrasts with the U.S. being the world’s second-largest video game market by revenue in 2024, highlighting the difference between a country’s gaming market size and the time its internet users spend playing.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## East Asia Shapes Gaming Culture, But Spends Less Time Playing
Some of the most surprising results come from East Asia, home to several of the world’s most influential video game industries.
South Korea averages 5 hours and 48 minutes of gaming per week, while China records 5 hours and 12 minutes. Taiwan comes in at 6 hours and 3 minutes, and Hong Kong at 5 hours and 6 minutes.
Japan ranks 53rd out of 54 markets, with internet users spending just 3 hours and 59 minutes gaming each week. That’s less than half the 9 hours and 9 minutes recorded in the United States.
Despite their global influence on gaming culture, all five East Asian markets fall below the worldwide average.
Japan’s position is particularly striking given its role in shaping the global gaming industry through companies such as Nintendo and Sony.
The contrast highlights an important distinction: producing some of the world’s most influential video games doesn’t necessarily mean spending the most time playing them.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## How Influencer Culture Varies Around the World
### Key Takeaways
*   Africa has the highest average influencer-following rate at 33.4%, with all five surveyed markets ahead of the United States.  
*   Only three of Europe’s 23 surveyed markets exceed the worldwide benchmark of 22.6%: Norway, Portugal, and Ireland.  
*   The Philippines has nearly three times Japan’s influencer-following rate, highlighting wide differences across Asia.
Influencer culture is often associated with the United States, home to some of the world’s biggest social media personalities and platforms. Yet following influencers is considerably more common in several countries across Africa, Asia, and Latin America.
Ghana leads the global ranking, followed by the Philippines and Brazil. Meanwhile, the U.S. sits well outside the top 10, despite its prominent role in global social media culture.
This visualization uses Q2 2025 data from GWI, published in the Digital 2026 Global Overview Report. It measures the share of social media users aged 16 and older who follow influencers across 53 countries and territories.

Humanity may have never finished building the Tower of Babel, but that hasn’t stopped us from building towering skyscrapers and magnificent monuments, particularly in the post-Industrial era.
How tall have these structures gotten? And when were they built?
We visualize the tallest statue on every continent (excluding Antarctica), along with where they are located and the year of its completion. Important to note: the height measurements include the foundation. Data is from a list of sources: World Famous Things, World Atlas, the Guinness World Records, and Britannica.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## Ranked: Towering Statues, by Continent
At a colossal 182 meters (597 ft), the **Statue of Unity** is the tallest in Asia—and the world—and is located in the Indian state of Gujarat.

Completed in 2018, it depicts Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, a key leader in the Indian Independence movement and India’s first deputy Prime Minister. His legacy—the political integration of India—lends the statue its name.
Portugal’s **Sanctuary of Christ the King** is the tallest in Europe, at 110 meters (361 ft). Inspired by Christ the Redeemer in Rio, the statue was completed in 1959 as an expression of gratitude for Portugal not suffering direct consequences from World War II.
Across the Atlantic, NYC’s famous **Statue of Liberty** is the tallest in North America at 93 meters (305 ft). A gift from the people of France, the structure originally shone a reddish-brown color. The current green visage is the result of the natural oxidation of its copper surfaces.
Rounding up, Senegal’s **African Renaissance Monument** (52m / 171 ft) and Venezuela’s **Monument to the Virgin of Peace** (47m / 154 ft) are the tallest in Africa and South America respectively.

## Brazil and Mexico Outgame U.S. Despite Massive Gaming Market
The Americas account for five of the top 10 markets, making the region particularly prominent in the ranking.
Brazil averages nearly two hours more gaming per week than the United States, while Mexico also ranks ahead of the U.S. at 9 hours and 24 minutes.
This contrasts with the U.S. being the world’s second-largest video game market by revenue in 2024, highlighting the difference between a country’s gaming market size and the time its internet users spend playing.

# Mapped: Every Continent’s Tallest Statue
## East Asia Shapes Gaming Culture, But Spends Less Time Playing
Some of the most surprising results come from East Asia, home to several of the world’s most influential video game industries.
South Korea averages 5 hours and 48 minutes of gaming per week, while China records 5 hours and 12 minutes. Taiwan comes in at 6 hours and 3 minutes, and Hong Kong at 5 hours and 6 minutes.
Japan ranks 53rd out of 54 markets, with internet users spending just 3 hours and 59 minutes gaming each week. That’s less than half the 9 hours and 9 minutes recorded in the United States.
Despite their global influence on gaming culture, all five East Asian markets fall below the worldwide average.
Japan’s position is particularly striking given its role in shaping the global gaming industry through companies such as Nintendo and Sony.
The contrast highlights an important distinction: producing some of the world’s most influential video games doesn’t necessarily mean spending the most time playing them.
